event.active_generic_land_03_mystery_aba: A voice whispers from the ditch and asks whether “the paper inspector” is gone.
Call for the campers
You follow an animal track onto a loose slope and slide through the stones.
You find a blanket stretched over a drainage opening where several people are holding their breath.
A false trail nearly brings you back to the fire before a muffled breath comes from the ditch.
The first clear trail vanishes into a ditch covered with fresh branches.
Choose the right trail
You knock over the hot pot and burn yourself before reading the tracks around the fire.
You spot knee and hand marks in the dirt: the campers crawled out of sight.
The camp was left in a hurry, but the tracks blur together in the dust.
All tracks leave the tents in one direction, without the heavy bags.
Read the hurried departure
A roadside camp looks deserted, but soup is still steaming, heavy bags lie open, and every pair of shoes is gone. Tracks circle the tents and then slide toward a rocky ditch.
The Camp Abandoned Too Fast
They explain that a fake inspector seized their papers, then returned demanding money. They hid when he came back.
Hear the campers out
In the brush, an abandoned satchel contains the group’s papers and several identical forms.
Recover the abandoned satchel
The group comes out and warns approaching travelers about the fake inspection. The camp becomes safe again instead of a silent trap.
Warn the next travelers
Beneath fresh branches, several campers hide in a drainage ditch. They left the fire burning to suggest a sudden departure and are watching the road.
Voices Under the Branches
event.active_generic_land_03_mystery_bor: Your tone shuts the conversation down; the traveler demands the papers back and tries to leave immediately.
Without threats, you get the reason: only one of the two names appears on local permits.
The traveler repeats one name and then the other without a coherent explanation.
The traveler admits both names are used depending on who controls entry.
Question them without accusing
You mix up the two receipts and give the traveler time to reclaim the important one.
Even the thumb ink smear appears in the same place on both receipts.
The dates overlap, but the names could still belong to two different people.
Both signatures share the same broken loop on the final character.
Compare the receipts
The traveler answers to both before catching themselves. Simple coincidence is no longer plausible.
Say both names aloud
Your silence is enough: the traveler puts both receipts on the table and stops pretending they belong to someone else.
Let the silence work
At a boarding house desk, a porter calls a traveler “Jessa” while the register says “Marlow.” Two receipts fall from their pocket, signed with both names on overlapping dates.
The Borrowed Name
The traveler finally gives their real name and explains using the other to pass a checkpoint that rejects their usual permit.
Ask for the real name
You return the papers after establishing that one person wrote both identities. The deception is understood without inventing a second suspect.
Return the receipts
The clerk corrects the register and will no longer vouch for the two names as separate guests.
Tell the clerk
Both receipts were written by the same hand: the same broken loop, pressure, and thumb smear. The traveler stops denying the use of two identities.
The Same Ink Loop
event.active_generic_land_03_mystery_cod: The signs match no official delivery route; instead, they line up with residents’ regular absences.
Lining up the symbols shows they always recur on houses closed at the same time.
You erase a fresh mark and wait. A man carrying a list passes that door without stopping.
Small chalk marks appear under several doors after each delivery round. Residents call it a courier code, but only homes that are regularly empty carry two strokes.
You move the symbols onto doors that are always occupied. The list carrier abandons the check after two bad stops.
The list pairs each symbol with an empty time window. The supposed delivery code was burglary scouting.
Residents erase the double strokes and change their routines before the next round.
After one symbol is erased, a man arrives with a list, checks the thresholds, and skips exactly the altered door. He carries neither parcels nor a delivery ledger.
event.active_generic_land_03_mystery_fal: You cite the wrong rule and briefly make the forged notice seem more credible.
The street does not even exist under that spelling in public records.
The wording feels wrong but gives you no clean proof.
The order uses a phrase dropped from official notices years ago.
Check the wording
You close one shutter and remain inside. The fake inspectors move as soon as the street appears empty.
Pretend to comply
You rub the seal and destroy part of the rim needed for comparison.
A cloth fiber is trapped in the wax: the stamp was molded from a badge, not a die.
The wax looks wrong, but the copy is clean enough to leave doubt.
The seal copies the official emblem but reverses two relief details.
Inspect the seal
You remove the sheet before the last shop closes. Two supposed inspectors watch the street from a handcart.
Take the notice down
A notice orders an entire block evacuated before dusk. The seal is the wrong color and the street name is misspelled, yet shops are already closing.
The Notice with the Wrong Seal
Shutters reopen. The fake inspectors abandon their handcart and leave their folder behind.
Call the residents back
They stop only at shops that already closed and compare their keys to the locks.
Follow the inspectors
The handcart carries key rings, blank forms, and numbering chalk, not inspection equipment.
Inspect the handcart
As several shutters close, two “inspectors” push a handcart down the street and test shop locks. Neither carries a named inspection register.
The Street They Wanted Empty
The key rings match the locks that were tested. You return them to the occupants before they can be reused.
Collect the duplicate keys
You have the cart and its contents recorded as evidence tied to the forged notice. The whole scheme now fits one coherent case.
Mark the handcart
The supposed warrants contain no names or addresses. The forged notice existed only to empty the street before break-ins.
Expose the blank forms
The abandoned folder contains unnamed “warrants,” lock impressions, and a list of shops that obeyed the evacuation. The motive for the forged notice is now obvious.
The Blank Warrants
The wheels pass behind the yard without ever entering it. The pennant was moved after the caravan left.
Follow the wheel tracks
The rope bears a mark from a thinner pole than the yard’s. The pennant was taken down elsewhere and rehung here.
Inspect the pennant knots
The teamster saw someone move the pennant after the real caravan passed. The travelers were waiting on a deliberately false signal.
Question the nearby teamster
A caravan pennant flies above an empty yard, and several travelers have waited there since dawn. Yet the wheel tracks pass behind the yard without ever crossing its gate.
The Pennant Without a Caravan
event.active_generic_land_03_mystery_foo: The first brick gives way and hits your wrist without opening anything.
The latch turns silently and immediately releases a pivoting brick panel.
You find several hollow bricks before an entire section shifts slightly.
The first knee-high stone turns like a latch.
Test the right brick
You trample the mud by the wall and erase the most useful shape.
You spot a clean mortar line directly under the final footprint.
The tracks truly end at the wall, with no useful return prints.
The last print points sideways, as if the foot pushed something.
Read the footprints
An entire section sounds hollow. Rain even outlines a vertical seam around the bricks.
Tap the wall
A crate vanished from a shop during the rain. Muddy footprints cross the yard, stop dead at a brick wall, and never return. The shopkeeper assumes a ladder was used.
Footprints to the Wall
You mark the outline before opening it. The mechanism can no longer be denied or quietly sealed again.
Mark the seam
The panel gives without breaking. On the other side, crate scrape marks cross the floor.
Push the panel
The wall pivots on a hidden axle and opens a passage wide enough for a crate.
Turn the brick latch
Rain outlines a perfect rectangle in the brickwork. A knee-high stone turns a quarter turn, and the whole wall section moves back a few centimeters.
The Pivoting Wall
The shopkeeper finally sees the full route. The “thief with no return tracks” never left ground level.
Leave the passage open
The stolen crate waits behind a neighboring storeroom. You return it and have the passage sealed from both sides.
Return the crate
The scrape marks lead to a service door and a hook still holding the rope used to pull crates through.
Follow the scrape marks
The panel opens onto an old service corridor between two buildings. The missing crate is still there behind barrels, with rope marks across its base.
The Shared Passage
event.active_generic_land_03_mystery_lau: All three keys were copied from the same master set: the file marks repeat exactly.
You remove the copies before they return to circulation. Wax in the hem explains how they were carried without a visible key ring.
The landlord recognizes two service doors. The third key opens a cupboard whose lock carries the same wax.
Show the keys to the landlord
A laundress finds three copied keys sewn into the hem of an unclaimed coat. None belongs to her shop, and one still carries soft wax between its teeth.
event.active_generic_land_03_mystery_mis: The sorter admits slipping the envelope into the slit to retrieve later, assuming the sealed sack would look untouched.
Question the sorter
The strap was fitted after sorting. The only possible time to remove the letter was before the clerk tightened the knot.
Reconstruct the tying order
One inner fold is thicker than the others. A slit beneath the strap allows a letter to be removed without touching the knot.
Count the sack folds
A mail sack arrives with knot and seal intact, but one envelope is missing from the inventory. The clerk who closed it insists no hand reopened the sack.
The Missing Envelope
The boots under the bench are still wet from the previous patrol. Their owner never resumed duty.
Check the boots
You accuse too quickly; the relief guard shuts down and alerts the whole post before answering.
The relief guard admits signing for him and immediately points out where he hid.
The relief guard claims ignorance but keeps glancing toward the supply room.
The relief guard admits to “covering five minutes” that turned into an hour.
Question the relief guard
You mistake an old correction for the fraud and delay the innocent relief shift.
The same ink splash physically connects both signatures: they were written in one sitting.
The signature is recent, but the roster alone does not show who held the pen.
The ink pressure matches the guard signed in directly above.
Analyze the watch roster
The night watchman is missing from his post, yet his name was just signed into the roster. His boots remain under the bench and the signature ink is still wet.
The Watchman Who Signed
You have the linked entries marked. The relief guard can no longer claim they were written at different times.
Mark both signatures
The watchman is asleep behind crates. His colleague signed for him to hide an absence that lasted too long.
Open the supply room
Woken in front of the roster, the guard immediately admits the forged signature and the arrangement between the two posts.
Wake the watchman
Under the lamp, the same ink droplet touches both consecutive names. The relief guard keeps glancing at the supply room, whose door is held shut by a crate.
The Two Signatures
event.active_generic_land_03_mystery_shu: A voice answers from the neighboring storeroom. The apprentice locked the workshop to use the absent master’s tools in secret.
The bar did not fall by itself: a string runs through a hole into the adjoining store. The “inside” lock was operated remotely.
The sawdust runs under a side panel and ends at a second door hidden behind shelving.
A workshop remains barred from inside while its owner is away. A neighbor heard hammering an hour ago, the furnace is cold, and a thin line of sawdust runs beneath a side partition.
event.active_generic_land_03_mystery_sti: You follow the wrong column and blame the wrong clerk; the counter loses more time.
You find the same discrepancy on an earlier page: the trick has been used before.
The sums still balance, but you cannot find where the three cargoes vanished.
Three carryovers were moved into a blank column before the page was stitched back in.
Recalculate the totals
You have the ledger laid flat and ask that nobody touch it until the lining is opened.
Close the ledger
You pull too hard and tear the page edge before reading the stitch pattern.
Carbon dust under the knot betrays a copied sheet hidden in the cover.
The thread is recent, but nothing yet shows who reopened the ledger.
The same flat knot also closes the inner lining of the cover.
Inspect the thread
An accountant freezes three payments: a ledger page was restitched with fresh thread, three cargoes are missing, yet the totals still balance. The clerk swears nothing was erased.
The Restitched Ledger
The recent additions match the accountant, not the clerk. The ledger was altered afterward to cover the diversion.
Compare the handwriting
A carbon copy preserves the three removed lines. All carry the same dock initials.
Open the lining
The clerk gets the proof that clears him. Payments can resume without a new ledger or another improvised accusation.
Give the copy to the clerk
Under the lining, a folded carbon sheet reproduces the page from before it was stitched. The three missing lines remain, with initials added in the margin.
The Copy in the Cover
event.active_generic_land_03_mystery_sto: The transaction stops before money changes hands. The seller must show what actually creates the declared weight.
Demand opening before payment
You tip the crate and break part of the goods that are actually inside.
You locate four identical masses in the corners beneath a very thin layer of goods.
The contents move as one mass without revealing how the weight was distributed.
A dense weight slides beneath a floor that sounds higher than the outer base.
Listen to the shift
You pick a normal crate and the unnecessary opening costs you compensation.
You pick the crate with a loose false bottom; a stone shows without breaking the seal.
The first crate is sound; the second finally makes the same stone thud.
The first test crate already hides a doubled base beneath the visible spices.
Pick a test crate
A sealed crate weighs exactly what the manifest says, but something heavy slides into one corner when it moves. The buyer refuses to open before payment; the seller pushes to close.
The Crate That Weighs Right
The false bottom hinge shows heat marks: stones could be loaded without touching the top seal.
Inspect the warm hinge
Four stones occupy most of the volume. A thin layer of goods merely hid the ballast.
Lift the false bottom
Without the stones, the goods make up only a fraction of the billed weight. The fraud becomes measurable.
Weigh the real contents
Beneath the visible spices, an inner board lifts by a centimeter. Its edge carries fresh heat marks, and a stone thuds directly below.
The False Bottom
event.active_generic_land_03_mystery_swa: All tags were shifted together except one room tag whose string was freshly tied.
Compare the tags
The bellhop admits shifting the board to enter one specific room without taking its key in front of the clerk.
Question the bellhop
A chalk mark behind the board shows where every key sat before the shift. One room remains deliberately wrong.
Restore the keys to their hooks
At an inn, every key on the board has shifted one hook. A guest opened the wrong room and found luggage under another name; the clerk swears the board was correct this morning.
Swapped Rooms
You stop both departures. Nobody receives the wrong cargo while the seals are checked.
Hold both carts
You break an intact seal while testing it and must compensate the sender.
The wax reveals a second heating: the seals were removed and reapplied.
Both stamps look authentic despite their absurd placement.
Both stamps carry the same tiny chipped star on the rim.
Inspect both seals
You transpose two lot numbers and hold another correct cargo by mistake.
You also spot an impossible minute: the same seal was logged at two doors at once.
The numbers match on paper, but the cart order still makes no sense.
The weighing times show the two crates switched carts after inspection.
Cross-check the manifest
Two carts ready to leave carry the right numbers but the wrong seals: medicine is marked as lamp oil, lamp oil as medicine. Both drivers blame the manifest.
Swapped Seals
The press is locked pending review. The trick used to swap cargo cannot be repeated immediately.
Have the press locked
The same flaw appears on a spare office stamp: someone used the local press to remake both seals.
Match the chipped star
The carts leave with their contents correctly identified and the false seals set aside.
Restore the correct labels
In the light, both seals show the same star-shaped chip. A spare stamp behind the desk carries exactly the same flaw.
The Chipped Star
event.active_generic_land_03_mystery_swe: The bed slides exactly into the clean rectangle and reveals a scratched board against the wall.
The scratch ends under molding that sinks when pressed.
A steady breath lifts dust beneath the molding. There is an occupied space behind the wall.
A room abandoned for weeks is covered in dust except for a perfectly clean rectangle beneath the bed. A fresh scrape runs from that rectangle to the wall molding.
You wedge the mechanism open. The hiding place can no longer vanish behind a bed pushed back into place.
A voice answers behind the wall and pushes the receipts out. The supposed abandonment concealed recent occupancy.
The panel hides a niche with blankets, food, and the former tenant’s stolen receipts. The room was still being used as a hideout.
The molding gives way and reveals a low door. Behind it, a niche holds fresh blankets, meal scraps, and papers the former tenant claimed were lost.
event.active_generic_land_03_mystery_thr: The gatekeeper received only one official notice and does not recognize the other two.
Two notices imitate the same hand, but the numerals lean differently.
Under the still-wet paste, a fourth notice appears with its time crossed out.
Three identical notices cover the same gate, but each schedules the district inspection at a different hour. Residents are already scattering, and the paste on the newest sheet is still wet.
You circle the ink and numeral errors. The neighbors can now tell which sheets were added after the cancellation.
The official cancellation is visible again. The false schedule immediately loses its effect.
A trail of paste leads to an alley where a bucket and two blank notices were abandoned.
The oldest sheet is the official notice: the inspection was canceled. The two newer sheets were pasted over it to empty the street at different times.
event.active_generic_land_03_mystery_tur: The detour ends in a muddy ditch and you lose a few Berrys recovering your things.
The wrench still carries a tag from the nearby tollhouse.
The track seems empty until a tool glints beneath a hedge near the toll road.
You immediately find a wrench abandoned near the rotated marker base.
Follow the first wrong turn
You reset one arrow the wrong way and send another traveler toward the detour.
Only one detour consistently benefits from the false markers: the nearby toll road.
You identify the tampering but cannot immediately recover the original orientation.
Maps and stone shadows let you restore every arrow to its original bearing.
Reconstruct the directions
You realign the arrows using wear marks on their bases. Travelers resume the direct road.
Set the arrows back
Several travelers reach the crossroads from the wrong direction. The stone arrows were rotated on their bases overnight, and the only consistent detour leads toward a toll road.
Turned Waymarkers
The spacing matches exactly. The arrows were turned with this tool, not by wind or accident.
Match the jaws to the bases
Travelers see the tag before taking the direct road again. The reason for the false detour becomes public.
Leave the tool in plain sight
The tag links the tool to the tollhouse. The marker bases carry fresh scars matching its jaws.
Show the tagged wrench
Under a hedge, a heavy wrench is still coated with dust from the marker base. A maintenance tag from the tollhouse hangs from its handle.
The Tollhouse Wrench
event.active_generic_land_03_mystery_two: You put both witnesses on the defensive; each adds details just to protect their story.
Separating their accounts gives the same detail: the sleeve changed color at the corner.
They remain certain about opposite colors and the discussion goes in circles.
They still describe the same gait, height, and torn sleeve.
Cross-question them
You follow a paint splash to a freshly painted wall and waste time.
The scrap also carries the same sleeve tear described by both witnesses.
The bench holds several colored fibers, but no clear direction.
A red fiber and a blue fiber are stitched back-to-back in the same scrap of cloth.
Inspect the corner bench
In the middle alley, you find a button painted red on one side and blue on the other.
Search the alley between them
A courier lost a satchel at the crossroads. A baker swears the thief wore red heading east; a porter says blue heading west. Both remember a torn sleeve.
Two Witnesses, Two Colors
The pocket contains the cut satchel strap and an unnamed storage ticket.
Check the pocket
The courier leaves with a consistent description, proof of the disguise, and a usable lead.
Give the coat to the courier
The coat is reversible: red on one side, blue on the other. Both witnesses saw the same person.
Turn the coat inside out
Behind a barrel, you find a coat discarded in haste. The lining is blue, the outside red, and the same sleeve is torn through both layers.
The Two-Sided Coat
event.active_generic_land_03_mystery_war: You open a flour store that collapses over you and covers the best tracks.
The counterweight drops by itself and reveals a hidden lift behind the sacks.
You search several empty hiding places before finally hearing a creak overhead.
The first panel you test hides a counterweight linked to the rafters.
Check the right hiding place
You step on a loose board and hurt yourself before finding the useful signs.
You also spot a rope still moving behind the sacks, with no draft to explain it.
The warmth confirms a recent departure, but not where everyone went.
Sole marks climb stacked sacks toward the rafters.
Read the signs of occupancy
In the silence, a pulley ratchet answers the still-warm brazier. Someone is above.
Stand perfectly still
A warehouse owner finds the building shut, the brazier still warm and the ledger open, but no handlers in sight. The rear door is bolted from inside and a delivery is waiting outside.
The Still-Warm Warehouse
The pulley stops. The foreman eventually comes down, unable to take the falsified labels with him.
Block the pulley
Voices answer from the rafters: the handlers hid after catching the foreman changing labels.
Call the handlers
The lift brings down the foreman with a cargo seal and three labels he was swapping out of sight.
Lower the lift
Behind the sacks, a small platform rises toward the rafters. A boot shows briefly above, then someone tries to jam the rope.
The Moving Pulley
event.active_generic_land_03_mystery_wax: The trunk scrapes the floor and reveals fresh dust fallen from the ceiling.
Move the trunk
You crush the wax and damage the mechanism; the innkeeper hands you the bill.
You also spot a fine fiber running from the keyhole toward the ceiling.
You spot marks, but only after scratching the lock.
The wax holds a clean impression of a key removed after locking.
Read the marks on the lock
You overheat the sample and erase the only useful impression.
You identify two layers: an older impression covered just before the disappearance.
The wax came from the inn, but you cannot tell how it was used.
The wax matches the hallway candles: someone prepared the impression on site.
Compare the wax to the candles
An innkeeper opens a room meant to be empty: fresh wax fills the lock, the window is still bolted from inside, and the guest is missing. The trunk, however, has not moved.
Wax in the Lock
In the loft, you find a wax key copy and a shifted roof tile: the locked room was staged.
Climb into the loft
You leave the hatch untouched. The innkeeper finally understands how the guest left without using the hallway.
Preserve the evidence
The thread releases a ceiling service hatch. Sole marks lead toward the roof.
Pull the thread
After moving the trunk, a waxy thread appears in the dust. It climbs the wall and vanishes into a ceiling seam directly above the bed.
The Ceiling Thread
